tools.description:
Execute a `bash` command. Use this for shell semantics — pipes, env, processes, git, package managers, build/test runners, anything genuinely interactive or multi-step.

**Translate these to a dedicated tool instead:**
- `cat` / `head` / `tail` (known path) → `Read`
- `sed` / `awk` (in-place edit) → `Edit`
- `echo > file` / `cat <<EOF` → `Write`
- `find` / recursive `ls` to locate files by name pattern → `Glob` (plain `ls <known-directory>` is fine for listing a directory)
- `grep` / `rg` (search file contents) → `Grep`
- `echo` / `printf` (talk to the user) → just output text directly

The dedicated tools render in the per-tool permission UI and keep raw stdout out of the conversation; that is why they are worth reaching for whenever one fits.

**Output:**
The stdout and stderr will be combined and returned as a string. The output may be truncated if it is too long. If the command exits non-zero, the output ends with a `Command failed with exit code: N` line; a command killed by its timeout or interrupted by the user ends with its own message instead.

Background execution is disabled for this agent. Do not set `run_in_background=true`.

**Guidelines for safety and security:**
- Each shell tool call will be executed in a fresh shell environment. The shell variables, current working directory changes, and the shell history is not preserved between calls. To run a command in a particular directory, pass the `cwd` argument (or use absolute paths) rather than relying on a `cd` from an earlier call.
- The tool call will return after the command is finished. You shall not use this tool to execute an interactive command or a command that may run forever. For possibly long-running commands, set the `timeout` argument in seconds. The default is 60s; foreground commands allow up to 300s; a foreground command that hits its timeout is killed.
- Avoid using `..` to access files or directories outside of the working directory.
- Avoid modifying files outside of the working directory unless explicitly instructed to do so.
- Never run commands that require superuser privileges unless explicitly instructed to do so.

**Guidelines for efficiency:**
- Use `&&` to chain commands that genuinely depend on each other, e.g. `npm install && npm test`. Independent read-only commands (separate `git show`, `ls`, or status checks) should be issued as separate parallel Bash calls in one response, not chained into a single call — chaining serializes their execution and mixes their output. Do not stitch outputs together with `echo` separators.
- Use `;` to run commands sequentially regardless of success/failure
- Use `||` for conditional execution (run second command only if first fails)
- Use pipe operations (`|`) and redirections (`>`, `>>`) to chain input and output between commands
- Always quote file paths containing spaces with double quotes (e.g., cd "/path with spaces/")
- Compose multi-step logic in a single call with `if` / `case` / `for` / `while` control flows.
- Do not set `run_in_background=true`; background task management tools are not available.

**Commands available:**
The following common command categories are usually available. Availability still depends on the host, so when in doubt run `which <command>` first to confirm a command exists before relying on it.
- Navigation and inspection: `ls`, `pwd`, `cd`, `stat`, `file`, `du`, `df`, `tree`
- File and directory management: `cp`, `mv`, `rm`, `mkdir`, `touch`, `ln`, `chmod`, `chown`
- Text and data processing: `wc`, `sort`, `uniq`, `cut`, `tr`, `diff`, `xargs`
- Archives and compression: `tar`, `gzip`, `gunzip`, `zip`, `unzip`
- Networking and transfer: `curl`, `wget`, `ping`, `ssh`, `scp`
- Version control: `git`; for GitHub-hosted work (PRs, issues, CI runs, API queries) prefer the `gh` CLI when installed — it carries the user's GitHub auth and can return structured JSON
- Process and system: `ps`, `kill`, `top`, `env`, `date`, `uname`, `whoami`
- Language and package toolchains: `node`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `python`, `pip` (use whichever the project actually relies on)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description:
Find files by glob pattern, sorted by modification time (most recent first).

Powered by ripgrep. Respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` by default — set `include_ignored` to also match ignored files (e.g. build outputs, `node_modules`). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) are always filtered out. Matches are files only — directories themselves are never listed; to find a directory, glob for a file inside it (e.g. `**/fixtures/**`).

Good patterns:
- `*.ts` — all files matching an extension, at any depth below the search root (a bare pattern without `/` matches recursively)
- `src/*.ts` — files directly inside `src/` (one level, not recursive)
- `src/**/*.ts` — recursive walk with a subdirectory anchor and extension
- `**/*.py` — recursive walk from the search root for an extension
- `*.{ts,tsx}` — brace expansion is supported
- `{src,test}/**/*.ts` — cartesian brace expansion is supported too

Results are capped at the first 100 matching paths. If a search would return more, a truncation marker is appended. Refine the pattern (extension, subdirectory) when 100 is not enough, or call again with a narrower anchor.

Large-directory caveat — avoid recursing into dependency / build output even with an anchor, especially when `include_ignored` is set:
- `node_modules/**/*.js`, `.venv/**/*.py`, `__pycache__/**`, `target/**` can produce thousands of results that truncate at the match cap and waste context. Prefer specific subpaths like `node_modules/react/src/**/*.js`.

path.description: Directory to search. Accepts an absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory. Defaults to the current working directory.

include_ignored.description: Also match files excluded by ignore files such as `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` (for example `node_modules` or build outputs). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) remain filtered out for safety. VCS metadata directories (`.git` and similar) are always skipped, even when this is true. Defaults to false.

import struct, zlib, sys

def decode(path):
    d = open(path,'rb').read()
    assert d[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n'
    pos = 8; w=h=None; idat=b''; ctype=None
    while pos < len(d):
        ln, = struct.unpack('>I', d[pos:pos+4]); typ = d[pos+4:pos+8]
        data = d[pos+8:pos+8+ln]; pos += 12+ln
        if typ==b'IHDR':
            w,h,bd,ctype,comp,filt,inter = struct.unpack('>IIBBBBB', data)
        elif typ==b'IDAT': idat += data
        elif typ==b'IEND': break
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    ch = 4 if ctype==6 else 3
    stride = w*ch
    px = bytearray(w*h*ch)
    prev = bytearray(stride)
    p = 0
    for y in range(h):
        f = raw[p]; p+=1
        line = bytearray(raw[p:p+stride]); p+=stride
        if f==1:
            for i in range(ch,stride): line[i]=(line[i]+line[i-ch])&0xff
        elif f==2:
            for i in range(stride): line[i]=(line[i]+prev[i])&0xff
        elif f==3:
            for i in range(stride):
                a=line[i-ch] if i>=ch else 0
                line[i]=(line[i]+((a+prev[i])>>1))&0xff
        elif f==4:
            for i in range(stride):
                a=line[i-ch] if i>=ch else 0
                b=prev[i]; c=prev[i-ch] if i>=ch else 0
                pp=a+b-c
                pa,pb,pc=abs(pp-a),abs(pp-b),abs(pp-c)
                pr = a if (pa<=pb and pa<=pc) else (b if pb<=pc else c)
                line[i]=(line[i]+pr)&0xff
        px[y*stride:(y+1)*stride]=line
        prev=line
    return w,h,ch,px

def pixel(px,w,ch,x,y):
    i=(y*w+x)*ch
    return tuple(px[i:i+ch])

if __name__=='__main__':
    w,h,ch,px = decode(sys.argv[1])
    print('size',w,h,'ch',ch)
    if len(sys.argv)>2:
        # x,y pairs
        for a in sys.argv[2:]:
            x,y=map(int,a.split(','))
            print((x,y), pixel(px,w,ch,x,y))
EOF

# 08 — Rendering options (pixel-probed, scale-factor 1)

Probe setup: PNG decoded with pure Python. Unless noted, all renders use the auto-generated
default config (passed explicitly via `--config` to isolate from concurrent processes;
verified byte-identical to no-`--config` output). Reference input `code3.txt` =
`aaa bbb ccc\nddd eee fff\nggg hhh iii\n`.

## Baseline geometry (default config, scale 1)
- 3-line file → image 518×344. Window bg `#282a36` bbox x 82..435, y 82..189.
- Margin 82 all sides (config `window.margin`). Window has 1px border (#ffffff30 blended
  over bg → pixel (81,82,92)) and rounded corners (radius 12).
- Mac bar: circles at y 92..108 (10px dia.), x 99..108 / 115..124 / 131..140,
  colors (255,94,87), (255,186,46), (43,200,65). Bar adds 24px.
- Code: left padding 17px from window edge (first glyph ink at x=99), char advance ≈7.4px,
  line height 18px (line n strip y = 120+18·(n−1) .. +17), code text color #f8f8f2,
  digit cap height 10px. First code glyph row y=123 (cap) / ink rows 124..132 for line 1.
- Min image width 518 (window min content width ~354); window grows with content, never wraps.
- Background default: horizontal linear gradient #6bcba5 (left edge) → #caf4c2 (right edge),
  constant vertically (corners: (0,0)=(107,203,165), (517,0)=(202,244,194), same at bottom).
- Watermark default "CodeSnap" (config font Pacifico → fallback), pure-white ink bbox
  (199,242)-(319,281), centered on image x=259, sitting in bottom margin below window.
- Error log lines (e.g. `[ERROR] ...`) go to **stdout** (not stderr), always with ANSI:
  `\x1b[31m[ERROR]\x1b[0m <msg>\n`, even with `--silent` and when redirected. Rust panics go
  to stderr, exit 101. Clean `[ERROR]` exits are 1. clap usage errors exit 2.

## (a) Line numbers (`--has-line-number`)
- Flag takes no value (`--has-line-number false` → clap "unexpected argument").
- Digits drawn in the code font, color default `#495162` (verified pixel (73,81,98)),
  starting exactly where code would start (x≈99), **right-aligned** in a gutter field:
  - 12-line file: 1-digit numbers ink x 108..112, 2-digit ink x 100..113 (same right edge).
- Digit field right edge by max digit count d: d=1→104, d=2→113, d=3→121, d=4→129
  (≈ +8.3px per extra digit). Code start: d=1→118, d=2→128, d=3→136, d=4→145
  (base code start 99; gap between digit right edge and code ≈ 14–15px).
- No separator line between gutter and code. Window width unchanged while within min width.
- `--line-number-color '#ff0000'` → pure (255,0,0) digits. Alpha in the hex is IGNORED
  (`#ff000080` still renders (255,0,0)). Invalid color (`red`) → panic
  `Invalid hex color: red` at core/src/utils/color.rs:32, exit 101.
- `--start-line-number`: default = 1 (render equals `--start-line-number 1`).
  0 is accepted (numbers 0,1,2). Negative rejected by clap (u32):
  `error: invalid value '-3' ...: -3 is not in 0..=4294967295`, exit 2.
  Gutter width is based on the largest *displayed* number (start + lines − 1).
- `--start-line-number` without `--has-line-number` → no effect (byte-identical to base).

## (b) `-d/--delete-line`, `-a/--add-line`
- Each value is a **range string** (same syntax as --highlight-range): `-d 2`, `-d 1:2`,
  `-d 2:` all work. Multiple values: both space-separated (`-d 1 3`) and repeated flag
  (`-d 1 -d 3`) work and produce byte-identical output.
- Strip geometry: full window interior width x 84..433; line n strip y = 120+18·(n−1),
  height 18 (line 1: 120..137, line 2: 138..155, line 3: 156..173). Strips for adjacent
  lines merge contiguously. Strip also covers the line-number gutter area.
- Colors: default delete `#ff6b6b30` → blended pixel (81,54,64) over #282a36;
  add `#2ecc7130` → (42,72,65). Custom `--delete-line-color`/`--add-line-color` honor alpha
  (`#0000ff80` → (20,21,155); `#00ff00` → opaque (0,255,0)).
- Both on same line: delete drawn first, add on top → (75,82,73) (verified blend order).
- Deleted-line text is NOT styled: no strikethrough, no dimming (text pixels stay #f8f8f2).
- Line numbers refer to **absolute file lines** (with `--range 5:10`, `-d 5` highlights the
  first displayed line; `-d 1` errors).
- Errors (stdout, `[ERROR]` prefix, exit 1):
  - out of range high: `The highlight end range should be less than or equal to 3`
  - zero: `The highlight start range should be greater than or equal to 1`
  - with --range 5:10, `-d 1`: `The highlight start range should be greater than or equal to 5`
  - negative: `invalid digit found in string`

## (c) Highlight ranges
- `--highlight-range 2:4`-style; **both ends inclusive** (2:3 highlights lines 2 and 3,
  strip y 138..173 = 36px). Open ends work: `2:` (2..end), `:2` (start..2). Reversed `3:2`
  is accepted and normalized to min..max (renders lines 2..3). Non-numeric →
  `[ERROR] invalid digit found in string` (exit 1). End beyond last line →
  `[ERROR] The highlight end range should be less than or equal to 3`.
- Strip geometry identical to delete/add strips: x 84..433, y = 120+18·(n−1), 18px/line,
  contiguous merge. Default color `#ffffff10` → blended (54,56,67).
- `--highlight-range-color '#ff0000'` → opaque red strip (alpha honored).
- Without `--range`, absolute line numbers = displayed lines. With `--range 5:10`:
  absolute range must lie inside 5..10 (`2:3` → error `... greater than or equal to 5`);
  `--relative-highlight-range` makes values 1-based over the *displayed* lines
  (`2:3` relative = file lines 6..7). Without `--range`, relative flag changes nothing
  (byte-identical output).
- `--raw-highlight-lines` = JSON array; each entry is either `[line, "#color"]` or
  `[start, end, "#color"]` (untagged enum `HighlightLine`). Verified
  `[[1,"#ff0000"],[3,5,"#00ff00"]]`: line 1 → opaque red strip (120..137), lines 3..5 →
  green but clipped to existing line 3 only (156..173), no error. Reversed `[2,1,color]`
  normalized to 1..2. Line 0 / beyond-end entries silently clipped, exit 0. `[]` → exit 0.
- Malformed JSON errors (all stdout `[ERROR]`, exit 1, exact texts):
  - `not json` → `expected ident at line 1 column 2`
  - `[[1,2]]` → `data did not match any variant of untagged enum HighlightLine at line 1 column 7`
  - `[1,"#ff0000"]` → same variant error at column 3
  - `[["x","#ff0000"]]` → same at column 17
  - `[[-1,"#ff0000"]]` → same at column 16
  - `{"a":1}` → `invalid type: map, expected a sequence at line 1 column 0`
  - valid JSON but bad color `[[1,"red"]]` → **panic** `Invalid hex color: red`
    (core/src/utils/color.rs:32), exit 101.

## (d) Breadcrumbs (`--has-breadcrumbs true|false`, default false)
- Adds exactly 15px height (2-line file: 326 → 341; 3-line: 344 → 359).
- Breadcrumb line occupies the slot directly under the mac bar; glyph rows y 122..133
  (cap height ~11–12px), starts at code x=99; code shifts down 15px.
- Content = the file path **verbatim as passed to `-f`**: relative stays relative
  (`sub/deep/file.py` ink x 99..208), absolute stays absolute (ink x 99..328).
  `-c` + `--file-path sub/deep/file.py` renders **byte-identical** to `-f` of that path.
- `-c` without `--file-path` → breadcrumb line omitted entirely (no height added,
  byte-size equal to breadcrumbs-off render).
- `--breadcrumbs-separator`: replaces every `/` in the path with the given string
  (separator `....` widened ink to x 99..251 for 2 slashes). Default `/`.
- `--breadcrumbs-color '#00ff00'` works (default #80848b from config).
- `--breadcrumbs-font-family`: changing to an installed font (DejaVu Sans) produced
  identical output here (default CaskaydiaCove Nerd Font already falls back); no error
  for missing fonts.

## (e) `--title`
- With mac bar (default): title drawn **centered in the mac bar** (window center x=259;
  "MyTitle" ink x 240..278, y 98..107). No height change (image stays 518×344).
- Without mac bar: title gets its own ~14px strip at top (ink y 96..105), still centered;
  image height +14 vs no-bar-no-title (334 vs 320), code shifts +14.
- No truncation: a 120-char title widens window to 814px (image 978 wide); title ink
  (x 66..910) is ~30px wider than the window body and overflows symmetrically onto the
  margin (not clipped). 300 chars → image 2058 wide, title ink 3..2053 — canvas grows to
  fit, still no clipping observed.
- Defaults from config: color #ffffff (pure white ink verified), font Pacifico (fallback
  here). `--title-color '#ff0000'` works. `--title-font-family` exists.

## (f) `--mac-window-bar false` (clap possible values exactly `true`/`false`; `yes` → error)
- Removes the 24px bar and circles entirely: image 518×320 (−24), code first ink row
  moves 124 → 100 (top padding inside window = 18px in both modes). Nothing replaces the
  bar — plain window bg. Title still renders in its own strip (see e).

## (g) Watermark
- Default content "CodeSnap" (from config `watermark`). Centered horizontally on the image
  (center x=259), vertically in the bottom margin (glyph bbox y 241..282, ~41px tall for
  the fallback font at scale 1; window bottom at 190, image bottom 344).
- `-w ''` → no watermark, no error (image identical to default except watermark region).
- Long text (80 chars): not wrapped; stays centered and is **clipped by the canvas**
  (ink spans x 7..517, y 241..343, cut at right/bottom edges); image size unchanged.
- `--watermark-color '#ff0000'` works (same geometry, red ink).
- `--watermark-font-family 'DejaVu Sans'` changes rendering (ink bbox widens to
  x 184..333); missing fonts silently fall back.

## (h) Shadow (`--shadow-radius`, `--shadow-color`)
- Defaults from config: radius 20, color #00000040. Shadow is cast around the window onto
  the background; canvas size never changes with radius (0 → 518×344, 50 → 518×344).
- radius 0 removes shadow entirely (pixel at (60,130): (118,208,168) = pure gradient vs
  (114,201,162) with default shadow). radius 50 → wider/softer darkening ((112,197,159)).
- Floats accepted (`12.5` ok). Negative accepted and clamped to 0 (`-5` byte-identical
  to radius 0).
- `--shadow-color '#ff0000'` → red shadow (pixels (136,180,146), (155,154,125)).
  Invalid color (`red`) → panic `Invalid hex color: red`, exit 101.

## (i) `--background`
- CLI flag is **silently ignored** in all tested forms: `#112233`, `"#112233"`, full
  gradient JSON (`{"start":{"x":0,"y":0},"end":{"x":"max","y":0},"stops":[...]}`),
  `{"color":...}` variants, bare `112233`, and garbage — exit 0, output byte-identical
  to default gradient. No validation error ever.
- Via **config file** (`snapshot_config.background`): both a plain string (`"#112233"` →
  uniform solid fill, verified (17,34,51)) and the gradient object work. Gradient object:
  `{"start":{"x":0,"y":0},"end":{"x":0,"y":"max"},"stops":[{"position":0,"color":"#ff0000"},
  {"position":1,"color":"#0000ff"}]}` → vertical red→blue ("max" = full extent along axis).
  Default config gradient start (0,0) end ("max",0) = horizontal.

## (j) Input handling
- Tabs: expanded to a **fixed 2 character cells** (not tab stops, not 4): `a\tb` puts b at
  char cell 3, `ab\tc` c at cell 4, `abc\tc` at cell 5 (measured x 121/128/135).
- Trailing whitespace: kept — window widens to include it (60 x's + 40 spaces → image 929
  wide vs 636 without).
- CRLF: `\r` stripped/normalized — `one\r\ntwo\r\n` renders byte-identical to LF version.
  CR-only (`one\rtwo\r`) also splits into 2 lines → both `\r\n` and lone `\r` are line breaks.
- Trailing blank lines: content is split into lines and **one** trailing empty line is
  dropped (min 1 line): `a\n`→1, `a\n\n`→1, `a\n\n\n`→2, `a\n\n\n\n`→3, `a\nb\n\n\n`→3,
  `\n`→1, `\n\n\n`→2. (Heights: 308 = 1 line, +18 per extra line.)
- Empty input (0-byte file or `-c ''`): renders fine — min-size 518×308 image with one
  empty line, exit 0.
- Very long lines: never wrapped — 500-char line → image 3859 wide, exit 0.
- `-c` with no value reads the snippet from **stdin** (byte-identical to rendering the same
  text from a file).
EOF
